fixes.explanation: Messengers, yes, friend. Verse 16 says, “At the sight of them, she lusted for them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.” She saw pictures on a wall and sent word across the distance. It all started with what she saw.
That's right. Verse 17 says that after the Babylonians defiled her, “…she turned away in disgust.” The Babylonians came to her, and afterward she was the one who turned away from them.

True. In verse 18 God says, “…I turned away from her in disgust, just as I had turned away from her sister.” That comes right after she openly prostitutes herself and exposes her nakedness. Both sisters ended up in the same place with Him.

Yes. Verse 30 says, “…because you have prostituted yourself with the nations and defiled yourself with their idols.” Verses 29 and 30 together say her indecency and promiscuity brought these things on her. God spells out the reason Himself, so we don't have to guess.

Yes. Verse 35 says, “Because you have forgotten Me and have cast Me behind your back, you must bear the consequences of your indecency and prostitution.” God puts it in His own words. Two phrases carry it: forgotten Me, and cast Me behind your back.

Moab is a fine guess, friend, but the text never puts the sisters there. Verse 3 says, “…and they played in Egypt, prostituting themselves from their youth.” Egypt is the place God names, so this one sends us back there.
Edom doesn't show up anywhere in this passage. God points to Egypt: “…and they played in Egypt, prostituting themselves from their youth.” That's the land where it all began for these two sisters.
Shechem is a fine guess, but God doesn't name it here. Verse 4 says, “…Oholah is Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem.” The younger sister is Jerusalem. Shechem just isn't the city on this page.
Jericho is the city whose walls fell down (Joshua 6:20), but God doesn't use it in this picture. Verse 4 says, “…Oholibah is Jerusalem.” That's the city where Judah's kings reigned (1 Kings 14:21).

Weapons make sense with warriors on horseback, friend. But verse 7 says, “She defiled herself with all the idols of those for whom she lusted.” The verse names idols as what defiled her, and weapons aren't mentioned there.

Treasures is a shiny guess, but shiny isn't what verse 7 says. It says, “She defiled herself with all the idols of those for whom she lusted.” The word on this page is idols, and that's what defiled her.
False is right. Verse 10 says her lovers “…seized her sons and daughters, and put her to the sword.” Seized, not protected. It's a heavy verse, so take a breath here, friend.

Verse 12 says, “She too lusted after the Assyrians…” She went after Assyrian governors, commanders and horsemen, just like her sister. Verse 13 says it outright: “both of them had taken the same path.” So True is the answer here.
Gifts is a kind guess, friend, but nothing in verse 16 hands anybody a present. It says, “At the sight of them, she lusted for them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.” The word is messengers.

It would be nice if memory worked that way. Verse 19 says, “Yet she multiplied her promiscuity, remembering the days of her youth…” She remembers, and she multiplies. Nothing in the verse says she turns back, so this one is False.
False is right. Verse 19 says, “Yet she multiplied her promiscuity, remembering the days of her youth…” She remembers, and she multiplies. Nothing in the verse says she turns back.
Verse 22 says otherwise, friend. God says, “…I will bring them against you from every side…” Not one side, every side. That's the picture God gives.

Verse 27 doesn't say that. God says, “So I will put an end to your indecency and prostitution, which began in the land of Egypt…” The thing that ends is the indecency and prostitution. Her name isn't mentioned in that verse.

A line of kings sounds weighty, friend, but verse 27 doesn't go there. God says, “So I will put an end to your indecency and prostitution, which began in the land of Egypt…” That's the one thing He says He will end. Kings never come up in that verse.

Taking over her sister's land sounds like a reason somebody might give, friend, but verse 31 doesn't. It says, “Because you have followed the path of your sister, I will put her cup into your hand.” The reason in that verse is the path, and land never comes up.

Never hearing His word is a tempting guess, but it isn't what God says. Verse 35 says, “Because you have forgotten Me and have cast Me behind your back, you must bear the consequences of your indecency and prostitution.” The reasons He gives are forgetting Him and casting Him behind her back. Hearing never comes up in that verse.
